items.mainDefect: Office365 event creation always uses the first destination calendar instead of the one matching the current credential, so secondary hosts in collective bookings write to the organizer's calendar.

secondary.defect: Lark and the base calendar service have the same problem: they always pick the first destination calendar instead of matching it by credential.

items.mainDefect: When a reference has no externalCalendarId, the Google Calendar update fallback looks for a destination whose externalId matches that missing value, so updates leave out the calendarId.

secondary.defect: When the reference has no externalCalendarId, the matching Google Calendar delete fallback targets the primary calendar, so events in secondary calendars are never deleted.

items.mainDefect: When externalCalendarId is absent, the Google Calendar update fallback looks for a destination matching that missing value and cannot find a real one, so updates lose their calendar ID.

secondary.defect: The deletion fallback at lines 315-317 has the same flaw, so deletions go to the primary calendar instead of the configured non-primary calendar.
